 Ahoi Ashtami 2026 falls on November 1, although the Ashtami Tithi continues until November 2. Check the puja muhurat, star-sighting time, vrat rituals and significance.

 Ahoi Ashtami is being observed on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with women observing a day-long fast and praying for the well-being of their children. However, the festival's date may cause confusion because the Ashtami Tithi continues into November 2. According to the Hindu calendar, the vrat falls on November 1. From the evening puja muhurat to the time for sighting stars, here is what devotees need to know.
 Ahoi Ashtami 2026: Why is the Vrat on November 1? 
 Ahoi Ashtami is observed on the eighth day of Krishna Paksha in the Hindu month of Kartik. This year, the Ashtami Tithi begins at 2:51 PM on November 1 and ends at 1:10 PM on November 2.
 Despite the Tithi extending into the following day, the festival will be celebrated on November 1, as the evening worship falls on this date.

 According to the New Delhi Panchang, the Ahoi Ashtami puja muhurat will be from 5:36 PM to 6:54 PM on November 1. Devotees can perform the evening rituals during this period and offer prayers to Ahoi Mata.
 Ahoi Ashtami 2026: Star Sighting and Moonrise Time 
 Sighting stars is an important part of the Ahoi Ashtami observance. In New Delhi, stars are expected to become visible at approximately 6 PM on November 1. Women traditionally offer arghya to the stars and conclude their fast after completing the evening rituals.
 Some families, however, follow the custom of breaking the fast after sighting the Moon, which is expected to rise at around 11:40 PM.
 How do women observe Ahoi Ashtami? 
 The day begins with women taking a fasting vow. Some observe a nirjala vrat, avoiding both food and water until the evening rituals are completed. In the evening, they prepare a place for Ahoi Mata's worship and offer flowers, roli, rice, sweets and other traditional items.
 The Ahoi Ashtami Vrat Katha is recited as part of the puja. The fast is completed according to the family's traditional practice, usually after offering arghya to the stars.
 Why is Ahoi Ashtami celebrated? 
 Ahoi Ashtami is observed mainly by mothers in North India, who pray for the long life, good health and happiness of their children. The festival is dedicated to Ahoi Mata, and its rituals are associated with maternal devotion and the well-being of the family.
 Women also observe the vrat while praying for the blessing of children. The festival holds particular importance in Hindu households, where the Ahoi Mata Vrat Katha forms an essential part of the evening worship.
